visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video begins with a medium shot of a female host with long, dark hair, wearing a white, cream, and brown panelled sweatshirt. She stands against a dark blue background with a geometric line pattern, gesturing with her right hand while speaking directly to the camera. (2) A quick cut shows a montage of b-roll: first, a bald man looking into the camera with a child on his shoulders, followed by a close-up of a hand with hair growing on the palm. These clips are framed within a smaller window over the host's background. (3) The scene returns to the host in her studio setting, where she continues her explanation, using expressive hand gestures and facial expressions to emphasize her points about a new scientific discovery from National Taiwan University regarding hair growth. (4) The visual transitions to scientific diagrams and a research paper titled 'Adipocyte lipolysis activates epithelial stem cells for hair regeneration...'. These graphics are clear and informative, showing cellular processes. (5) Another sequence of b-roll appears, featuring a person washing their hair under a shower, and then a chart comparing hair growth on the skin of mice over twenty days. The mice are shown from a top-down perspective, highlighting the increase in hair coverage. (6) The host is shown again, now describing the types of fatty acids involved, like palmitoleic and oleic acid, found in fish and olive oil. Visual overlays of oil being poured and a pipette applying serum to a hand accompany her narration. (7) Finally, a clip of a man with thick, wavy hair is shown as he runs his hands through it, before cutting back to the host for her closing remarks and a call to action, maintaining her energetic and engaging presence.
